page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-64 is a compute-oriented virtual machine built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance is powered by an ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core). Cache hierarchy includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and an 80 MB shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 128 GB RAM, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server has no bundled local storage and includes zero integrated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional multi-threaded computing capability and high memory subsystem throughput. In synthetic and real-world multi-core benchmarks, the server scored 26,801 on Geekbench multi-core and 116,240.18 on multi-core stress-ng tests. Large block uncached memory throughput achieved 345.92 GB/sec for reads and 190.24 GB/sec for writes. The architecture excels in developer tooling, evidenced by a Clang software compilation score of 85,520, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 719.88 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput reaching 123.05 GB/sec. Redis operations also demonstrated top-tier performance at over 134 million SET operations per second.

Cost efficiency is driven by high execution density across dedicated ARM cores, providing substantial throughput per compute resource compared to legacy x86 architectures. However, architectural tradeoffs exist: the instance lacks bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all persistence relies on network-attached storage disks. Furthermore, x86-specific vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX are not present, requiring applications to target native ARM64 or NEON instructions.

The c4a-highcpu-64 instance is suited for compute-heavy, multi-threaded workloads that fit comfortably within a 2 GB per core footprint. Recommended workloads include large-scale CI/CD build farms, native ARM software compilation, static web server fleets, distributed caching tiers like Redis, and batch compression or decompression pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-64 is a compute-focused instance powered by 64 dedicated ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 3.0 GHz. Designed with a 1:2 core-to-memory allocation, it provides 128 GB of system RAM, 80 MB of L3 cache, and hardware AES acceleration, while omitting integrated GPUs and local storage. Benchmark results place this machine in the upper tier for multi-threaded processing, evidenced by 26,801 in Geekbench multi-core, an 85,520 Clang compilation score, and uncached memory read bandwidth exceeding 345 GB/sec. It also demonstrates high throughput in network serving and Redis in-memory transactions. Because persistent storage relies entirely on external network volumes and memory is constrained to 2.0 GB per core, this instance is tailored specifically for compute-dense workloads. It represents an efficient platform for distributed code compilation, CI/CD runners, parallel batch processing, high-volume web serving, and caching infrastructure.
